Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. Attaching the first-pass hero and a short procurement note for our marketplace team (files attached). Before we lock the listing, two quick questions we need your help on: 

1) Metering unit — we currently bill customers on vCPU-hours inside our SaaS offering. For AWS Marketplace, would you recommend mapping to:vCPU-hour SKU OR a custom "inference-unit" that better matches token/throughput? Any implications for private offers?

2) Co-sell badge & evidence — what minimal telemetry / field artifacts does Redwood need to surface co-sell approvals in the listing? We can share a stub SOC2 paragraph if that helps.

Attached: acme-hero-draft.docx, procurement_requirements.pdf

Appreciate your help — happy to hop on a 30-min call if it’s easier.

Best,
Sarah Kim
Head of GTM, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Draft hero + metering question for AWS listing

Thanks Sarah — good questions. Quick notes below and next steps.

Short answers:
- Metering: we generally recommend an "inference-unit" SKU for inference-heavy products — maps better to customer expectations and preserves flexibility for private offers. We can still expose mapping to vCPU-hours in the procurement docs for customers that require infra-level billing.
- Co-sell evidence: minimal set we need: product one-pager, SOC2 & data-retention statement, and a short demo/video link we can surface in the field. If you already have a SOC2 blurb in procurement_requirements.pdf that should be fine.

Action items:
- Jonas: can you validate the metering recommendation against our AWS metering templates and confirm any entitlements knobs?
- Marissa: please review the hero doc and suggest two alternate taglines we can use for A/B.
- Sarah / Raj: can you add a 30-min slot Thursday 9–11am PT or Friday 8–10am PT for a quick marketplace handoff?

I attached our internal quick guide for marketplace listings (redwood-marketplace-guidelines.pdf) — contains SKU examples and suggested private-offer language.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple technical notes from the metering/offer side — replying with suggestions inline.

> On Wed, Apr 10, 2029 at 11:05 AM, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Metering: we generally recommend an "inference-unit" SKU ...

Agreed with Sergio. A few practical considerations for AWS Marketplace metering:
- If you publish a usage-based listing, prefer a single "inference_unit" metric tied to calls/sec or token-equivalent. This gives predictable unit economics when customers run inference at scale.
- For private offers: include a secondary mapping table in the offer docs: 1 inference_unit = 0.5 vCPU-hour (example) so procurement teams can reconcile internal chargebacks.
- Entitlements: make sure the product SKU exposes an entitlement for "burst_capacity" (boolean) if you plan to offer burst in Dedicated deployments.

Hero copy: two quick, different tones (Marissa, feel free to pick):
- Option A (field-facing): "Deploy LLM-powered features with predictable latency & cost — Redwood Inference on AWS Marketplace."
- Option B (technical): "High-throughput LLM inference with batching, KV caching, and cost controls — deploy via AWS Marketplace."

Procurement footnote suggestion (to add to procurement_requirements.pdf):
""
Redwood Inference will provide a usage mapping table and a formal private-offer billing appendix upon request. Standard evidence: SOC 2 attestation, data-retention policy, and deployment architecture diagram.
""

Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1xMarketGuidelines (contains example mapping table)

Happy to jump on the Thursday slot if that works — I'm free 9:30–10:30am PT.

Jonas Weber
Product Partnerships Lead | Redwood Inference
